NL_main_result: For subgroups `H, K ≤ G`, the double-coset quotient `H \ G / K` is finite if and only if there exists a finite collection of cosets in this quotient whose double-coset preimages cover `G`.

For a continuous `R`-linear equivalence `f : M ≃L[R] N` and any submodule `s : Submodule R M`, the closure of the image `s.map f` equals the image under `mapEquiv f` of the closure of `s`. In other words, "closure of image = image of closure" through a continuous linear equivalence.

Let `Y` be a standard Borel space and `κ : Kernel X Y` a Markov kernel. Then there exists a jointly measurable map `f : X → I → Y` such that for every `a : X`, the pushforward of the uniform measure `volume` on the unit interval `I` by `f a` equals `κ a`.

Let `c` be a complex shape on an index type `ι` with an `EulerCharSigns` instance, and let `X` be a graded `R`-module object with `finrank R (X i) = 0` for every `i` outside a given finite set `s`. Then the `finsum` Euler characteristic equals the explicit finite sum: `eulerChar c X = ∑ i ∈ s, (χ i : ℤ) · finrank R (X i)`.

Let `S` be a flat `R`-algebra and consider a commutative diagram with exact rows ``` M₁ --f--> M₂ --g--> M₃ | | | i₁ i₂ i₃ v v v N₁ --f'-> N₂ --g'-> N₃ ``` where `f, f'` are injective. If `i₂` and `i₃` exhibit `Nₖ` as the base change of `Mₖ` from `R` to `S`, then so does `i₁`.

Let `α` be a densely-ordered linearly-ordered topological space and `β` a `T₂` regular space. If `f : α → β` is continuous on the unordered open interval `uIoo a b` (where `a ≠ b`) and tends, within `uIoo a b`, to the same limit `l` as the argument approaches either endpoint, then `f` attains a global extremum on `uIoo a b` at some interior point `c ∈ uIoo a b`.

Let `E` be a real locally convex topological vector space (with `𝕜 = ℝ` or `ℂ` providing the affine functionals), `s ⊆ E` a closed convex subset, and `φ : E → ℝ` a function that is convex and lower-semicontinuous on `s`. Then the family ``` 𝓕 := { f : s → ℝ | f ≤ φ|_s ∧ f = (Re ∘ l)|_s + c for some l ∈ E →L[𝕜] 𝕜, c ∈ ℝ } ``` of affine minorants of `φ|_s` has supremum equal to `φ|_s`.

Let `f : ℂ → ℂ` be holomorphic on the open ball `‖z‖ < R` with `f 0 = 0`, and assume `Re (f z) < M` for every `z` in the ball (with `0 < M`, `0 < R`). Then for every `z` with `‖z‖ < R`, ``` ‖f z‖ ≤ 2 M ‖z‖ / (R − ‖z‖). ``` (The general Borel–Carathéodory bound `borelCaratheodory` follows by applying this to `f − f 0` after enlarging `M` to `M + ‖f 0‖`; see field 8.)
Let `f : ℝ → E` be continuous on `[a, b]` and differentiable on `(a, b)`, with `‖f'(t)‖ ≤ B(t)` for almost every `t ∈ (a, b)` and `B` interval-integrable on `[a, b]`. Then

Let `p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄` be points in a real Euclidean affine space with `p₁ ≠ p₂`. If `p₃` bisects the oriented angle `∡p₁p₂p₄` (i.e. `∡p₁p₂p₃ = ∡p₃p₂p₄`) and `p₃, p₄` lie on the same (strictly defined) side of the line through `p₁` and `p₂`, then the unoriented angle satisfies

Let `L` be a first-order language, `M` an `L`-structure, `A ⊆ M` a parameter set, `β` a finite type, and `F : (α → M) → (β → M)` a *definable map* over `A` (each coordinate `v ↦ F(v)(i)` is a definable function over `A`). For every `A`-definable set `S ⊆ (β → M)`, the preimage `F⁻¹(S)` is `A`-definable.
Let `M` be a C¹ manifold modelled on `(E, H, I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H)` with `n ≠ 0`. Then `I.interior M = { x : M | extChartAt I x x ∈ interior (range I) }` is open.

Let `P : ℝ[X]` have `deg P ≤ n` and satisfy `|P(x)| ≤ 1` for all `x ∈ [-1, 1]`. Then for every `k ∈ ℕ` and every `x ≥ 1`, `(P^{(k)})(x) ≤ (T_n^{(k)})(x)`, where `T_n` is the `n`-th Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.

Let `F = (F_t)` be a right-continuous filtration on `ι` (a conditionally complete linearly-ordered first-countable densely-ordered space with no maximum), and let `(τ_n)_{n : κ}` be a countable family of stopping times for `F` with values in `WithTop ι`. Then `ω ↦ ⨅_n τ_n(ω)` is again a stopping time.
Fix `k : ℕ`. Let `p : ℕ → ℝ` be a sequence with `n · p_n → r`. Then `(n choose k) · p_n^k · (1 − p_n)^{n − k} → e^{−r} · r^k / k!`.

Let `A` be a normed ring and `v : A →+* ℂ` an isometry. For every polynomial `p ∈ A[X]` and every `n : ℕ`, `‖p.coeff n‖ ≤ binomial(deg p, n) · M_v(p)`, where `M_v(p) := mahlerMeasure (p.map v)` is the generalised Mahler measure.

Let `p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄, p` be points in a real inner-product affine space `P`. Suppose `p` lies strictly between `p₁` and `p₂` and strictly between `p₃` and `p₄` (so `∠ p₁ p p₂ = ∠ p₃ p p₄ = π`), and that `p₁, p, p₃` are not collinear. If `dist p₁ p · dist p₂ p = dist p₃ p · dist p₄ p`, then `{p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄}` is cospherical.
For any complex polynomial `p ∈ ℂ[X]`, `Σ_{i ∈ supp p} ‖p.coeff i‖² = (1 / 2π) ∫₀^{2π} ‖p(e^{iθ})‖² dθ`. That is, Parseval's identity on the unit circle, read coefficient-wise.

Let `M` be a structure for a first-order language `L`, and let `A ⊆ M` be a subset that meets every nonempty `L`-definable subset of `M`. Then the substructure of `M` generated by `A` is an elementary substructure.
For `n, m : ℕ` with `n ≠ m`, `∫ (T_n(x) · T_m(x)) / √(1 − x²) dx = 0`, where the integral is taken on `(−1, 1]` against the weighted Lebesgue measure `μ_T = 1_{(−1,1]} · (1 / √(1 − x²)) dx`.
Let `R` be a ring, `v : R → ℝ` a non-archimedean absolute value, and `c > 0` a real number. Then for any `p, q ∈ R[X]`, `gaussNorm v c (p · q) = gaussNorm v c p · gaussNorm v c q`.

Let `ρ : Representation k G V` and `σ : Representation k G W` be irreducible monoid representations of `G` on `k`-vector spaces. Then any intertwining map `f : ρ → σ` is either the zero map or a bijection.
For every location `x₀ : ℝ` and positive scale `γ > 0`, the Cauchy probability density `x ↦ (πγ)⁻¹ · (1 + ((x − x₀)/γ)²)⁻¹` integrates to `1` over `ℝ`.

Let `f : α → β` and `g : β → γ` be Scott-continuous on a domain family `D` of subsets of `α` (resp. `D'` of `β`). Suppose `D` is closed under two-element subsets `{a,b}` (with `a ≤ b`) and that `f` sends `D`-sets to `D'`-sets after image. Then `g ∘ f` is Scott continuous on `D`.
Let `P ∈ ℝ[X]` and `x ∈ ℝ`. If every (real) root of `P` is strictly less than `x` and `P` has a non-negative leading coefficient, then `P(x) > 0`.
Over a Noetherian ring `R`, if `S` and `T` are CoFG submodules of an `R`-module `M`, then so is their intersection `S ⊓ T`.
The set of odd abundant natural numbers is infinite.

Let `R` be a Noetherian (commutative) ring, `M` an `R`-module, `N ⊆ M` a submodule, and `x ∈ M`. If `I` is a minimal prime over the annihilator-style ideal `N : {x}` (`= colon N {x}`), then there exists `x' ∈ M` with `I = N : {x'}`.
For every compact subset `K` of a topological space `α`, its powerset `K.powerset = {t : Set α | t ⊆ K}`, equipped with the (subspace of the) Vietoris topology on `Set α`, is compact.

Let `M` be a smooth manifold, `𝕜` a non-trivially normed field, and `V` a `𝕜`-normed space. Suppose `f : M → 𝕜` and `g : M → V` are maps having `HasMFDerivAt`-derivatives `f' : T_x M → 𝕜` and `g' : T_x M → V` at `x` (with both targets canonically identified with the corresponding tangent spaces via `NormedSpace.fromTangentSpace`). Then `f • g` has `HasMFDerivAt`-derivative `f x • g' + toSpanSingleton 𝕜 (g x) ∘L f'` at `x` (the standard product rule, after canonically identifying the tangent space to `V` at `(f • g) x` with `V`).

Let `M` be an `R`-module, `n : ℕ`, and `v : I → M` an indexed family with `I` linearly ordered. If the range of `v` spans `M`, then the family `(v(i₁) ∧ ⋯ ∧ v(iₙ))` indexed by ordered subsets `{i₁ < ⋯ < iₙ} ⊆ I` of size `n` spans the `n`th exterior power `⋀ⁿ M ⊆ ⋀M` (viewed as a submodule of the exterior algebra).
Let `f : ℝ → E` be a function and `μ` a measure on `ℝ`. For a function `b : ι → ℝ` and a filter `l` on `ι`, if `b → +∞` along `l`, then `∫_{Ioi (b i)} f dμ → 0` along `l`.
For every integer `n`, every `k ∈ ℕ`, and every real `x` with `|x| ≤ 1`, `|T_n^{(k)}(x)| ≤ T_n^{(k)}(1)` (where `T_n` is the `n`th Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind, real-valued).

Let `P` be an affine space over a strictly ordered ring `R` with model module `V`, and let `f : StdSimplex R (StdSimplex R P)` be a "simplex of simplices" (a probability distribution over probability distributions over `P`). Then the convex combination of the inner combinations equals the convex combination of the joint distribution: `convexCombination (f.map convexCombination) = convexCombination f.join`.

Let `G : SimpleGraph V` and `α, β` non-empty finite types. Then `K_{α,β}` (the complete bipartite graph) is contained as a subgraph of the bipartite double cover `G.bipartiteDoubleCover` iff it is contained in `G`.
For any Banach space `E` and any function `f : UnitAddTorus d → E`, and for any base point `a : d → ℝ`, `∫ x : UnitAddTorus d, f x = ∫ x in {x | ∀ i, x i ∈ (a i, a i + 1]}, f (fun i ↦ ↑(x i))`.

Let `u, b, c : ℕ → ℝ` with `0 ≤ u n₀`, `0 ≤ b n`, `0 ≤ c n` for all `n ≥ n₀`, and assume the recurrence inequality `u (n+1) ≤ (1 + c n) · u n + b n` for `n ≥ n₀`. Then for every `n ≥ n₀`, `u n ≤ (u n₀ + ∑_{k = n₀}^{n−1} b k) · exp (∑_{i = n₀}^{n−1} c i)`.
Let `α` be a commutative monoid with zero that is a unique factorization monoid. For any `a, b : α` with `a` and `b` coprime (`IsRelPrime a b`), `μ(a · b) = μ(a) · μ(b)`.

Let `f : P →ᵃ[k] P₂` be an injective affine map, `s` an affine simplex in `P`, and `I ⊆ k` a weight-set defining the "interior" of a simplex. Then the interior of the image simplex `s.map f hf` (with weights in `I`) equals the image under `f` of the interior of `s`: `(s.map f hf).setInterior I = f '' s.setInterior I`.

Let `R = (R i)` be a family of monoids and `B = (B i)` a family of submonoids (one in each `R i`), and let `𝓕` be a filter on the index set. An element `x : Πʳ i, [R i, B i]_[𝓕]` is a unit if and only if (i) `x i` is a unit in `R i` for every `i`, and (ii) eventually along `𝓕`, the value `x i` lies in `B i` and is a unit in the submonoid `B i`.
Let `R` be a commutative semiring and `A` an `R`-Hopf algebra with antipode `S` and multiplication `μ`. Then for all `a, b ∈ A`, `S(a · b) = S(b) · S(a)`.

Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor between sites equipped with precoverages `J` on `C` and `K` on `D` that are stable under base change and have pullbacks. If `F` preserves the (pairwise) pullbacks of every `J`-covering and the image of every `J`-covering under `F` is a `K`-covering, then `F` is continuous for the Grothendieck topologies generated by `J` and `K` — i.e. the pullback `F.op ⋙ G` of any sheaf `G` on `(D, K_top)` is a sheaf on `(C, J_top)`.

For finite measures `μ, ν` on `α`, finite kernels `κ, η : Kernel α β`, with `μ ⊗ₘ κ ≪ μ ⊗ₘ η`, the Radon–Nikodym derivative of `μ ⊗ₘ κ` with respect to `ν ⊗ₘ η` (as measures on `α × β`) is, almost everywhere with respect to `ν ⊗ₘ η`, equal to the product `p ↦ (dμ/dν)(p.1) · (d(μ ⊗ₘ κ)/d(μ ⊗ₘ η))(p)`.

Let `α` be any type and `β : α → Type*` with each `β a` finite. Suppose for every finite set `s : Finset α` we have a function `g s : (a : α) → β a`. Then there is a single function `χ : (a : α) → β a` such that for every finite set `s`, there exists `t ⊇ s` with `χ x = g t x` for every `x ∈ s`. Informally: the family of local guesses `(g s)` can be stitched into a global function `χ` that, on each finite set `s`, agrees with `g t` for some super-finite-set `t`.

For a magma `M`, the assignment `s ↦ mulCayley s` from `Set M` to `SimpleGraph M` is a left adjoint (a Galois connection): for every `S ⊆ M` and every simple graph `G` on `M`, `mulCayley S ≤ G ↔ S ⊆ {g ∈ M | ∀ a, a * g ≠ a → G.Adj (a * g) a}`. Equivalently, `mulCayley` is the smallest simple graph in which every element of `S` produces an edge from `a` to `a * g` (whenever distinct).

Let `J` be a precoverage on `C` such that the morphism property "is an isomorphism" is local at the target for `J`. Let `f, g : X ⟶ Y` be two morphisms over `S` and let `𝒰 = {Uᵢ → S}` be a `J`-cover of `S`. If for every `i` the base-changed maps `f ×_S Uᵢ = g ×_S Uᵢ : X ×_S Uᵢ → Y ×_S Uᵢ` agree, then `f = g`.

For an `n`-simplex `s` in an affine space over a linearly ordered field (with `n ≥ 1`), the closed interior of `s` is the union of its open interior and the closed interiors of its `n + 1` opposite faces: `s.closedInterior = s.interior ∪ ⋃ i, (s.faceOpposite i).closedInterior`.

In a triangulated category `C`, for any three object properties `P, Q, R` we have `extensionProduct (extensionProduct P Q) R = extensionProduct P (extensionProduct Q R)`, i.e. the extension product is associative as an operation on `ObjectProperty C`.
Let `F : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` be a Zariski sheaf. Then for any small index type `ι`, `F` preserves limits of shape `Discrete ι` — i.e. `F` carries arbitrary coproducts of schemes to products of types.
For a continuous `𝕜`-linear map `T : E →L[𝕜] F` between Hilbert spaces, `ker (T† ∘L T) = ker T`. (Axler 7.64(b).)

Let `(Aᵢ)_{i ∈ s}` and `(Bᵢ)_{i ∈ s}` be finite families of functions on a filter `l`. If for each `i` we have `Aᵢ =O_{Cᵢ}[l] Bᵢ` (i.e. eventually `‖Aᵢ x‖ ≤ Cᵢ · ‖Bᵢ x‖`), then the sum `∑ᵢ Aᵢ` is `O_{sup Cᵢ}[l]` of the function `∑ᵢ ‖Bᵢ‖`. The constant `sup Cᵢ` is the supremum of the individual constants over the index set.

Let `f : 𝕜 → E` be meromorphic. Then the pole counting function `r ↦ N(r, f, ⊤)` is `O(1)` (i.e. uniformly bounded for large `r`) if and only if the normal-form `toMeromorphicNFOn f univ` is analytic on all of `𝕜` — equivalently, every singularity of `f` is removable.
Let `f : ArithmeticFunction R` over a commutative ring `R`. Then `f` is a unit in the Dirichlet convolution ring iff `f 1` is a unit in `R`.

Let `G` be a group, `f : G →* G` an endomorphism such that `f(U) ⊆ U` for every subgroup `U`, and `h : G → ℝ` a height function. Suppose: a finite set `s` surjects onto `G ⧸ f(G)`; constants `0 ≤ a < b` and `c ≥ 0` satisfy `h x ≤ a · h(g·x) + c` for `g ∈ s`, `x ∈ G`, and `b · h x − c ≤ h(f x)` for all `x`; and every height-bounded set is finite. Then `G` is finitely generated.
For tuples `x, y : ι → K` over an admissible-absolute-value field `K`, the multiplicative height of the pointwise product satisfies `H(x · y) ≤ H(x) · H(y)`.

Let `E` be a real topological vector space, and let `s`, `t ⊆ E` be convex sets with `interior s` nonempty and disjoint from `t`, and `t` itself nonempty. Then there exist a *nonzero* continuous linear functional `f : E → ℝ` and a real number `u` such that `f a ≤ u` for all `a ∈ s` and `u ≤ f b` for all `b ∈ t`.

Let `R` be a commutative semiring. Equip `ArithmeticFunction R` with the topology of pointwise convergence (the discrete topology on each coefficient slot). Let `f : ι → ArithmeticFunction R` be a family such that for every `n`, `(f i) n = (1 : ArithmeticFunction R) n` for all but finitely many `i`. Then for every `n`, the partial products `∏ i ∈ s, f i` evaluated at `n` are eventually equal to `(eulerProduct f) n` as `s : Finset ι` grows along `atTop`.

Let a group `M` act on a set `V`, let `S` be a generator-index type with map `ι : S → M`, and form the Schreier graph `Γ := SchreierGraph V ι`. The labelling prefunctor `labelling : Γ ⥤q SingleObj S` is a *covering of quivers*: at every vertex `x : Γ`, the induced maps on stars and costars `Star_x → Star_{∗}` and `Costar_x → Costar_{∗}` are bijections.
The normalised derivative `D` satisfies the Leibniz rule on the upper half-plane: for `MDifferentiable` functions `F, G : ℍ → ℂ`, `D (F · G) = (D F) · G + F · (D G)`.

For a complex unital `*`-algebra `A` (with a `StarModule ℂ` and the obvious tower / commutation typeclasses), an element `x : A` is unitary iff it is star-normal and `(ℜ x)² + (ℑ x)² = 1`. (When one writes `x = a + i·b` with `a := ℜ x`, `b := ℑ x`, this is the familiar "`x` is unitary iff `a` and `b` commute and `a² + b² = 1`".)
Let `E` be a Hausdorff topological vector space over a complete non-trivial normed field `𝕜`. If `E` admits a totally bounded neighbourhood of `0`, then `E` is finite-dimensional.

Let `F ⊣ G : C ⥤ D` be an adjunction equipped with Grothendieck topologies `J` on `C` and `K` on `D`. Then `F` is cocontinuous from `J` to `K` (every `K`-cover of `F U` pulls back to a `J`-cover of `U`) if and only if `G` preserves covers from `K` to `J` (every `K`-cover of `X` is sent by `G` to a `J`-cover of `G X`).

Let `T : E →L[𝕜] E` be a compact self-adjoint operator on a complete inner product space `E`. Then the orthogonal complement of `⨆ μ, eigenspace T μ` (the closed span of all eigenspaces) is `⊥`, i.e. the eigenspaces of `T` together span a dense subspace of `E`.

Let `p : M →ₗ N →ₗ R` be a bilinear pairing between two `R`-modules and let `C : PointedCone R N` be a dually finitely generated cone (i.e. the dual w.r.t. `p` of some finite subset of `M`). Then `C` is recovered from its dual: `dual p (dual p.flip C) = C`.

Let `f : ℂ → ℂ` be analytic on the closed ball `B(c, R)`, satisfy `f c ≠ 0`, and `‖f z‖ ≤ M` on the sphere `∂B(c, R)` for some `M ≥ 1`. For any `r` with `0 < |r| < |R|`: the sum (with multiplicity) of the orders of zeros of `f` in `B(c, r)` is at most `log(M / ‖f c‖) / log(R / r)`.
Let `α` be a conditionally complete linear order with the order topology and let `f` be a non-trivial filter on `α`. If `f` is bounded and cobounded above, then `f.limsSup` is a cluster point of `f`.
For matrices `A, B : Matrix ι ι 𝕜` over an RCLike-scalar field, if `A` and `B` are positive semidefinite then so is their entrywise (Hadamard) product `A ⊙ B`.

For each `p ∈ (1,2)` there exists a positive scalar multiple `μ` of Lebesgue measure on `(0,∞)` such that for every `x ≥ 0`, the function `t ↦ rpowIntegrand₁₂(p,t,x) = t^{p−1}(x/t + t/(t+x) − 1)` is integrable for `μ` and `x^p = ∫₀^∞ t^{p−1}(x/t + t/(t+x) − 1) dμ(t)`.

Let `f : ℕ → Ω → E` be predictable with respect to a filtration `ℱ` and integrable at every step. Then its predictable part equals (almost everywhere) the increment process from time `0`: `predictablePart f ℱ μ n =ᵐ[μ] f n − f 0`.
